title: Enterprise-Class Cache Compression Design
problem: Physical size and latency constraints limit on-die cache capacity near processor cores, restricting memory hierarchy efficiency. Cache expansion is constrained by design limitations that prevent larger caches without latency penalties.
motivation: Effective cache capacity expansion via compression improves processor efficiency without violating physical design constraints.
method: Proposes inline data compression at lower-level caches using a custom scheme optimized for cache line-sized blocks. Analyzes optimal compressor/decompressor placement in the hierarchy, addresses common compression drawbacks, and presents a tiered design blueprint for product integration with prediction-assisted adaptive compression.
key_novelty: Prediction-assisted adaptive compression scheme specifically tailored for cache line-sized data blocks in enterprise processor hierarchies.
contributions: Custom compression scheme optimized for small cache line-sized data blocks
Analysis and optimization of compressor/decompressor placement strategies in cache hierarchy
Solutions to common compression drawbacks and practical implementation challenges
Tiered design blueprint for product integration in enterprise systems
limitations: Limitations not explicitly discussed in abstract; specific workload details and scope constraints not provided.
